bull_bear.body:
- Longstanding client relationships, financial strength and niche knowledge and expertise, which management states provides an edge for remaining relevant against domestic and international competitors
- Flexible engagement and pricing models - Time and Material (T&M) or Fixed Price Fixed Timeframe (FPFT) - together with a global delivery model proposed on the basis of the nature of work
- Centers of Excellence (COEs) that leverage talent skilled in specific technologies and domains, plus a Lab Model for temporary deployment of resources on one-time work
- Integrated IT plus infrastructure positioning - a strategic partner supporting both operational and infrastructural needs of client businesses
- Commercial property leasing business expected to provide a stable source of recurring income, supporting overall business stability
- Niche expertise providing clients innovative options for R&D spend, cost and time advantages, reduced integration risk and improved user productivity
- Internal control framework with a firm of Chartered Accountants appointed as Internal Auditors and quarterly reporting to an Audit Committee chaired by a Non-Executive Independent Director; internal financial controls confirmed adequate and effective as of March 31, 2026
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Cyber security and data-breach exposure — Increasing sophistication of cyber-attacks, data breaches and ransomware threats pose substantial risks to IT infrastructure and sensitive information - directly relevant since the Company runs collocation data centres, network support and cyber security offerings for clients.
- Regulatory compliance and data-privacy regulation — Stricter data privacy laws and regulations such as GDPR and CCPA require heavy investment in compliance, with significant penalties for non-compliance; the Company serves clients across geographies through subsidiaries in Germany and China.
- Rapid technological change and obsolescence — The fast pace of technological advancement can lead to obsolescence and requires continuous adaptation and investment to stay competitive.
- Talent shortage and retention — Growing demand for skilled IT professionals means the industry faces challenges attracting and retaining top talent, leading to skill gaps; talent retention is also flagged as an industry-level headwind in the business outlook.
- Competitive intensity, pricing pressure and market saturation — The Company faces an increasingly competitive landscape from domestic and international service providers, both large and small, while market saturation in certain segments can intensify competition and diminish margins, impacting profitability.
- Economic uncertainty and client IT budget cuts — Economic downturns or recessions can lead to reduced IT budgets, delayed investments and slower growth; changing customer spending patterns are separately flagged in the business outlook.
- Foreign exchange rate fluctuation — The rupee has exhibited two-way movements reflecting global and domestic factors, with protracted geopolitical tensions, heightened volatility in global financial markets and elevated global sovereign bond yields cited as ongoing drivers.
- Geopolitical and cross-border operating risk — Political instability, trade wars and regulatory changes in different regions can impact global operations and market access - relevant given overseas subsidiaries and international clients. The Company states it runs a well-defined and dynamic enterprise risk management (ERM) programme, governed by a comprehensive risk management policy and embedded in planning and review processes, to identify, record, track and mitigate such risks.

business.body: FCS Software Solutions Limited delivers technology-driven solutions including software development, digital marketing and end-to-end support services to corporate clients, serving businesses in Business Process Outsourcing (BPO), customized software development, e-learning and other technology-enabled services. It maintains client IT applications on a Time and Material (T&M) or Fixed Price Fixed Timeframe (FPFT) basis, using Centers of Excellence and a Lab Model for one-time work such as application testing and third-party application audit. Alongside its core IT offerings the Company is engaged in real estate management, leasing and letting out immovable property including IT infrastructure and commercial spaces, whether freehold or leasehold, to corporate entities, startups and service providers needing technologically equipped office space.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **IT & IT Enabled Services:** Software development, Digital marketing, End-to-end support services, Application Portfolio Support for Enterprise Applications, Infrastructure Management Services - collocation data centers, virtualization, system and networks support, plug and play infrastructure provisioning, WAN, IP based voice, cyber security, Customer-interaction services including call-centers, back office services, HR services, data entry and data conversion, content development and animation, transcription and translation, data search, market research, GIS, network consultancy
- **Education / E-Learning Services:** Content aggregation, Learning Management Systems, Portals, Assessment, Remote education
- **Leasing Services:** Leasing / letting out of immovable property including IT infrastructural premises, whether freehold or leasehold

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the core IT and ITES offerings and expand customer relationships
- Leverage emerging technologies where commercially viable
- Improve operational efficiency and pursue cost optimization / prudent cost management
- Use the commercial property leasing business as a stable source of recurring income to support overall business stability and long-term value creation
- Strengthen the core business, enhance corporate governance and implement prudent risk management practices for sustainable growth
- Engage clients through flexible commercial models - Time and Material (T&M) or Fixed Price Fixed Timeframe (FPFT) - and a global delivery model
- Operate Centers of Excellence (COEs) to concentrate talent in specific technologies and domains, and a Lab Model for one-time work such as application testing and third-party application audit
- The Company monitors capital on the basis of the carrying amount of equity less cash and cash equivalents as presented on the face of the balance sheet. Management assesses capital requirements in order to maintain an efficient overall financing structure while avoiding excessive leverage, taking into account the subordination levels of the Company's various classes of debt, and manages the capital structure with adjustments in the light of changes in economic conditions and the risk characteristics of the underlying assets. In order to maintain or adjust the capital structure the Company may adjust the amount of dividends paid to shareholders, return capital to shareholders, issue new shares, or sell assets to reduce debt, with a stated objective of providing an adequate return to shareholders. The Company has not declared a dividend in the current year or the previous year.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no specific capex project, capacity addition or expansion programme with a commissioning or ramp timeline. The Directors' Report states that there were no changes in the nature of the business of the company during the year under review, that there have been no material changes and commitments affecting the financial position of the company between the end of the financial year and the date of the report, and that there has been no change in the capital structure of the Company during the year. Expansion intent is expressed only qualitatively in the MD&A, where the Company says it intends to capitalise on industry opportunities by strengthening its core IT and ITES offerings, expanding customer relationships and leveraging emerging technologies where commercially viable, while expecting the commercial property leasing business to provide a stable source of recurring income. Existing group footprint referenced in the report comprises wholly owned subsidiaries in Germany and China, wholly owned Indian subsidiaries Insync Business Solutions Limited and Stablesecure Infraservices Private Limited, material subsidiary Bloom Healthcare and Hospitality Management Private Limited, and associate Enstaserv Eservices Limited; no new project or facility is announced for these entities.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The Indian IT industry continues to present significant long-term growth opportunities, supported by increasing digital transformation initiatives, growing cloud adoption, artificial intelligence, automation, cyber security requirements and rising demand for digital business solutions
- Enterprises across industries continue to invest in technology to improve productivity, customer experience and operational resilience
- Headwinds flagged by management: global economic uncertainties, pricing pressures, changing customer spending patterns, talent retention and rapid technological advancements
- Management expects the commercial property leasing business to provide a stable source of recurring income
- Outlook for 2026 described as increasingly optimistic, with inflation expected to moderate and fresh waves of innovation sparking renewed interest among consumers, investors and business leaders
- Breakthrough technologies such as generative AI, spatial computing and quantum computing are advancing rapidly and hold the potential to fundamentally transform how people live, work and innovate
- Increased focus on AI and automation technology is described as a great opportunity for outsourcing providers
- Competitive intensity is rising from domestic and international service providers, both large and small, with longstanding client relationships and niche expertise cited as the offset
